label: Editorial
title: The Rise of Chinese AI Short Drama
excerpt: In the space of about a year, AI-made microdramas went from a curiosity to the default way China's biggest short-drama platforms publish new titles — with some single launches now clearing nine figures in views within days.
body: China's short-drama industry didn't just grow in 2026 — its production method flipped. At a September briefing, the National Radio and Television Administration reported that roughly 430,000 microdramas were registered in the first eight months of the year alone, about 13 times the full-year total for 2025, and that AI-generated titles accounted for more than nine in ten of them. The same briefing put the national microdrama audience at 851 million people, a bit over two-thirds of the country's internet users.

Platforms built around the format scaled to match. Hongguo ("Red Fruit"), Douyin's dedicated short-drama app, reported roughly 600 million viewing sessions and 19.3 billion total views over this year's Lunar New Year period alone, with daily active users climbing past 160 million — more than double the figure from a year earlier. Those numbers don't distinguish AI-made titles from traditionally filmed ones, but they establish the scale an AI-generated hit is now launching into.

A handful of titles made the AI side of that shift concrete. Feng Shui Master, from the Chengdu studio behind it, reportedly passed 100 million views within 12 hours of its first season and has since run to a fifth season; Immortal Execution Platform — AI Live-Action Version, built on a 2025 web-comic IP, reportedly cleared 100 million views in six days and topped Hongguo's AI-drama chart; and The Heart Inside the Steamed Bun, made in China's "AI 漫剧" comic-drama style rather than live action, reportedly passed 1.3 billion views on Douyin. All three are in AIMB's catalog, alongside other recent AI-generated Chinese titles — browse them on the AI Short Drama page.

AIMB hasn't independently audited any of these figures — they're drawn from platform and trade-press reporting, not from a verified third-party measurement standard, and the short-drama industry doesn't yet have one. What's harder to dispute is the production-side shift: AI tools have pushed the cost and timeline of a short-drama season down far enough that a wave of title launches is now outpacing what a traditionally filmed pipeline could support, and the audience is showing up for at least some of what results.
